clue.text: A tyrannical man- Prospero's undoing

indicators.note: undoing the name unpicks its letters so they can be put together in a new order

parts.note: the name of Shakespeare's magician with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A tyrant brings about the downfall of Shakespeare's magician Prospero.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Prospero's counts as a letter: rearrange all nine letters, PROSPEROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rules cruelly and crushes those beneath him is a tyrant.

clue.text: Put the old boy up. It may well generate good feeling

definitions.text: It may well generate good feeling

parts.note: to put something somewhere is to place it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up tells you to read the word from bottom to top

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a former pupil a bed for the night, with a hint of goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' works because this is a down entry: the old boy is read upwards and attached to the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill works only through the patient's belief that it will help, so it makes them feel better.

clue.text: Italian church fantasy

parts.note: someone from Rome, the Italian capital, is a Roman
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A dream of something to do with Italy's church.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a fanciful, idealised story far removed from real life.

clue.text: Tot dealt with after damaging tiles using a sharp tool

indicators.note: after places the shuffled tot behind the shuffled tiles
damaging the word tiles breaks it up so its letters can be rearranged
the letters of tot are dealt out like cards into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A toddler has been dealt with by someone wielding a blade after breaking some tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams, signalled by 'damaging' and 'dealt with'; 'after' sets the toddler's letters behind the tiles' letters. 'Tot' looks like a child, but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a thin pointed dagger or a pointed instrument for making holes.

clue.text: Connect about fifty at one point

parts.note: re is Latin for 'in the matter of', meaning about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
E, for east, is one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: Joining up some fifty things at a single spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate two things is to link them or show how they are bound together.

clue.text: Take steps to bring the device into operation

definitions.text: Take steps to bring the device into operation

parts.words: Take steps to bring the device into operation
parts.note: taking steps sounds like acting to start a machine; read literally, walking is what makes this gadget count

explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer is a small instrument that counts the paces a walker takes.

clue.text: Hides away-a way remains

parts.note: ST, for street, is a way or road
ashes are what remains after burning, or after cremation

explanation.surface: Something tucked out of sight on a road where only cinders are left.
explanation.definitionFit: To stash something is to store it secretly in a safe place.

clue.text: A killer and degenerate admitted to an order

indicators.note: being admitted to a body puts one inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: the Garter is the highest British order of knighthood
to rot is to decay or degenerate

explanation.surface: A murderer and a reprobate are both made members of a knightly order.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotter kills by strangling the victim with a cord or wire.

clue.text: Choose a good artist to depict a Greek heroine

parts.note: to elect someone is to choose them by vote
RA, a Royal Academician, is an artist good enough to be elected to the Royal Academy

explanation.surface: Pick a fine painter to portray a heroine from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, daughter of Agamemnon, avenges her father's murder in Greek tragedy.

clue.text: The basis of hand-cream?

parts.note: the cream looks like a lotion for the hands; read again, the hand gives the first word and a creamy base the second

explanation.definitionFit: This tropical vegetable fat is pressed from palm fruits and used in soaps and cosmetics.

clue.text: A guy shaking a sourer cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A barman giving a sour drink a good shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: someone who shakes people up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who stirs up or excites others, shaking them out of calm, is a rouser.

clue.text: A real treat for vegetarians!

parts.note: taken literally, a celebration meal made of pulses would suit those who avoid meat; the phrase is in fact old slang for any jolly celebration

explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is British slang for a festive party or celebration, originally an annual dinner given by employers.

clue.text: The boss, that is deputy-head, is purposeful

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: head means the first letter of deputy

explanation.surface: An office hierarchy: the boss and the deputy head are both determined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' sounds like an employer but here means a raised knob, a STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A studied act is deliberate and done with careful intention.

clue.text: Flat tent housing Oriental people

indicators.note: housing means the tent holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written
E, for east, the region of the Orient
men means people

explanation.surface: A tent laid flat gives shelter to people from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an adjective for the tent, but it is the definition: a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into rented apartments, or one apartment in it.

clue.text: Most aggrieved, and therefore lie still

parts.note: so means therefore, as a result
to rest is to lie still

explanation.surface: Someone very upset, so they decide to lie quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean resentful or vexed, so the superlative is most resentful.

clue.text: The devil can cite for his purpose." (The Merchant of Venice)

definitions.text: The devil can cite for his purpose." (The Merchant of Venice)

parts.words: The devil can cite for his purpose." (The Merchant of Venice)
parts.note: a quotation from Shakespeare's play with a word left out, which the solver supplies

explanation.walkthrough: Antonio says in The Merchant of Venice that the devil can quote holy writ to serve his own ends; the missing word fills the gap after 'cite'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio's line names the sacred writings of the Bible, which the devil quotes for his own ends.

clue.text: Bit a lot? That's rubbish

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit
a heap means a lot, as in heaps of time

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a large helping as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded junk, and figuratively the place for what is thrown out.

clue.text: Suffer with cold-one will get better though

indicators.note: getting better means changing state, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A patient with a chill told that, though suffering, they will recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To condole is to share someone's grief and express sympathy.

clue.text: A little is dangerous!

parts.note: completes Pope's line from An Essay on Criticism that a small amount of knowledge is a dangerous thing

explanation.definitionFit: Pope warned that shallow knowledge breeds overconfidence; the missing word is acquired knowledge.

clue.text: Writing a note about a celebrity, a goddess

indicators.note: about means going round, so the other letters surround the celebrity

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Someone jotting a short message to a famous person and comparing her to a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: The remover takes ages with royal insignia

parts.note: eras are long ages of history
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher seen on post boxes

explanation.surface: A removal man taking away ages of regalia from the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser is a rubber, which removes pencil marks.

clue.text: A seaman set to clear up makes excuse

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to solve a mystery is to clear it up

explanation.surface: A sailor about to tidy up offers an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free someone from blame or pardon them.

clue.text: Get lean maybe for chic appearance

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dieter slimming down to look stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish in appearance.

clue.text: Trendy attitude for example

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a stance is an attitude or position on an issue

explanation.surface: A fashionable point of view offered as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something.

clue.text: Shows concern about a few graves

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to care is to show concern
V is the Roman numeral five, a few

explanation.surface: Someone grieving over several burial plots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graves' looks like burial plots, but here is the verb: to grave is to engrave, to cut into stone.
explanation.definitionFit: To grave is an old word for engraving, cutting a design into a hard surface.

clue.text: A director wants relatively modern furniture

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the more recent era as opposed to BC
a dresser is a piece of kitchen furniture with shelves

explanation.surface: A film or company director wants furniture that is fairly new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' is one who directs a letter, writing on it where it should go.
explanation.definitionFit: One who addresses a letter directs it to its recipient.

clue.text: The trainer will find drink dear in France

parts.note: tea is a drink
cher is the French word for dear

explanation.surface: A coach discovers that tea is expensive in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher instructs or trains pupils.

clue.text: Just a naughty boy

parts.note: Just ... is the title of Richmal Crompton's books about a mischievous schoolboy

explanation.definitionFit: The scruffy hero of Richmal Crompton's Just stories is a famously mischievous English schoolboy.

clue.text: Run over? Right, create commotion!

indicators.note: commotion is a disturbance that throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A driver who has hit someone is told to make a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace is to go back over the same ground again.

clue.text: Prepared for consumer who anticipates twisting

definitions.text: Prepared for consumer who anticipates twisting

parts.words: Prepared for consumer who anticipates twisting
parts.note: a dish cooked for a diner who expects to wind it round a fork

explanation.definitionFit: Long strings of pasta are eaten by twirling them round a fork.
